newsitem.title: SPAIN: Montoro says Spain can't be excluded from euro.
newsitem.headline: Montoro says Spain can't be excluded from euro.

text.p: Spanish Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said on Tuesday that it would be impossible to exclude Spain from the launch of Europe's single currency in 1999 given its solid economic credentials.
"With the passport we carry it isn't possible for anyone to say 'no'," Montoro told journalists.
He referred to a sharp improvement in inflation that fell to 2.5 percent in February, and a drop in long-term interest rates, now below seven percent.
"The countries of the south are proving we can do our homework," Montoro said.
Many countries are struggling to meet the five strict economic prerequisites for joining European economic and monetary union, prompting debate about whether to make the criteria more lax.
Montoro said Spain was not backing any relaxation of criteria.
"Spain isn't defending a lax interpretation of criteria. We are demonstrating that the criteria are advisable," Montoro said.
